native_result.query: How were the phases of the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE) characterized in terms of the first principal component in a PCA on the forms of capital analyzed in hundred-year time slices?
native_result.HypoA: During the Middle Neolithic (3400-3000 BCE) and Younger Neolithic (2900-2300 BCE), both phases are primarily associated with negative values on the first principal component (PC1). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In a PCA on the forms-of-capital variables analyzed in 100-year slices, PC1 (~30% of variance) characterizes both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) as POSITIVE, ELEVATED phases — high composite forms of capital relative to the overall series (mean ≈ 0) and clearly above the later Late Neolithic and Bronze Age phases (which turn negative). The Middle Neolithic is on average slightly higher (mean PC1 ≈ +1.39) with a rising trend through the phase (peaking ~3000–3200 BCE), while the Younger Neolithic is slightly lower (mean ≈ +1.13) and declines gradually toward 2300 BCE. So both Neolithic phases sit on the high-capital (positive PC1) side of the trajectory, with the Middle Neolithic marginally higher and rising and the Younger Neolithic marginally lower and declining, marking the onset of the long capital decrease that accelerates after 2300 BCE.
native_result.WorkflowB: Parsed capital.csv (comma decimals), kept all 12 Z-capital variables, treated the 39 rows as 100-year slices. Standardized each column (center+scale) and ran correlation-matrix PCA via eigen-decomposition (numpy; sklearn unavailable). Computed PC1 score per slice, assigned MN (3400–3000) and SG (2900–2300) by BCE (verified vs group column), and summarized per-slice values, mean±SD, within-phase linear slope, and relative magnitude vs the overall series and adjacent phases. Saved script and CSV tables as artifacts.
